goalsDialog.conclusionHint: The text players read when they win.
goalsDialog.rewardProgress: Conquest points for the completed objective
goalsDialog.eventWinHint: Victory comes from an event's "Win the adventure" effect (Events tool). The conclusion text and the points below are shown then.

goalsDialog.fillLaterHint: Enemy, conclusion and points can also be written later, but the Check asks for them. Texts are written in markdown:

chestsDialog.title: Chest rewards

chestsDialog.intro: When a hero opens a chest they randomly get one of the rewards listed below that matches the quality of the chest opened. For each reward set how much it gives of every prize with the − and + buttons (at 0 it gives none). You need at least one reward per chest plus any extra ones you want; you can confirm even with an incomplete table, the Check reports what is missing.
encounterDialog.title: Encounter token
encounterDialog.lookHint: An image from the token collection or an item's icon in place of the "?". The title is the token's name in the menu and in notifications.
encounterDialog.useHint: The hero stops on the square and picks the action from the "!" menu. Once used, the token disappears from the map (unless it is reusable): the events "A hero uses an encounter" and "The chosen encounters are no longer on the map" decide the consequences.
encounterDialog.flagsHint: Blocking movement and sight makes it like a rock (nobody passes through it or stops on it). If it is usable from adjacent spaces, the hero doesn't have to stop on it (walls and closed doors in between prevent it). If it is reusable it doesn't disappear after use and the events fire every time.
eventDialog.name: Name
eventDialog.messageHint: The text players read (markdown), with the "I've read it" button.
eventDialog.chooseGroundItem: Choose an item on the ground…
eventDialog.keyNameHint: The key's name, for example key-1
eventDialog.checkTextHint: The riddle or situation the hero reads before rolling (markdown).
eventDialog.endingHint: The text shown in the ending, after the adventure's conclusion (markdown).
eventDialog.moreTriggersHint: (if there is more than one, it is enough that one of them happens)
eventDialog.clearedEnemiesHint: Fires when the last of the chosen enemies (or of all of them, if the list is empty) is no longer on the map or in the area: defeated, removed or walked out. It does not fire if there were none at the start.
eventDialog.encountersGoneHint: Fires when the last of the chosen encounter tokens (or of all of them, if the list is empty) is no longer on the map or in the area, because it was used. It does not fire if there were none at the start.
eventDialog.onlyWhileInactive: Only while the enemy is inactive
eventDialog.onlyWhileInactiveHint: A "?" appears on the enemy and the adjacent hero finds the same option in the "!" menu. It can be done only once: then the "?" disappears.
eventDialog.evilTurnEndHint: Fires at the end of the Evil One's turn, after the monsters have played and before the next round begins. Usually used with a condition ("If"), for end-of-turn rewards and penalties.
eventDialog.onceHint: After the first firing the event never starts again, even if another trigger happens. An event whose conditions do not hold does not count as fired.
eventDialog.onceSingleHint: With a single trigger the event already fires only once. You can choose between "only once" and "every time" when there are several triggers ("or…") or the trigger can repeat, like "a chest is opened in an area".
eventDialog.addVariableCondition: Add a condition on a variable
eventDialog.addItemCondition: Add a condition on an item
eventDialog.modifyHint: It is added to the values it has for the rest of the game (negative to subtract).
eventDialog.removeHint: It leaves the map without loot and returns at full health on an already revealed free square, as far away as possible if none is far enough.
eventDialog.finishRevivalHint: If it is waiting to come back to life, its defeat is repeated now with the current variables. Otherwise it does nothing.
eventDialog.activateHint: If the enemy is inactive (set in Customize), from now on it acts like any other enemy; the stone look, if any, stays. Otherwise it does nothing.
eventDialog.removePieceHint: The enemy is removed from the map without being defeated: no loot and the "defeated" events do not fire.
eventDialog.vulnerableHint: From now on wounds count: the armor shows its number again. If the enemy is not invincible it does nothing.
eventDialog.lookHint: The old look fades out and the new one appears; "Normal" removes the look. The rest (inactive, invincible, immunities) does not change.
eventDialog.placeCatalogItemFirst: First put a catalog item on the map with the Items tool ("Catalog item" card).
eventDialog.moveItemHint: The token, already placed and customized on the map, moves to a random free square next to the start squares (not on the start squares). If the event does not fire it stays where you put it. Usually used with "The heroes reveal an area" on the starting area.
eventDialog.placeItemHint: The item appears on the ground on a random free square next to the start squares (not on the start squares). Usually used with "The heroes reveal an area" on the starting area. Whoever reaches it picks it up with "Pick up" in the "!" menu.
eventDialog.giveHint: It goes to the hero who triggered the event. A rune key (or a key) unlocks the doors for the whole party, and the Check counts it for rune doors. An item goes to them (if they have no room, it falls to the ground on their square); money goes to every hero, as in chests.
eventDialog.placeObstacleFirst: First put an obstacle with the Obstacles tool.
eventDialog.behaviorHint: The constraint applies from the Evil One's next turn, both for the script and for whoever plays it. "Normal" removes the behavior.
eventDialog.removeImmunityHint: It removes only this entry: the enemy's other immunities stay. "All states" does not touch, for example, an immunity to Flame alone that the enemy already had.
eventDialog.checkHint: The hero rolls as many proficiency dice as the extra dice of their chosen attack (with no dice the check fails, unless they buy some with energy); the difficulty is the number of sparks needed. By default they can spend 1 energy for each extra die before rolling; with "No energy for the dice" the button does not appear. With "Can be refused" Cancel also appears: nothing happens, the energy spent and the interaction cost come back and the "?" stays.
eventDialog.hatredHint: The Evil One gains (or, with a negative number, loses) this Hatred; it never goes below 0.
eventDialog.drawHint: The Evil One draws these cards from their deck, as at the start of the turn (if the deck runs out the usual penalty applies); the hand never exceeds the limit.
eventDialog.finalReward: Final Conquest points of the objective:
eventDialog.endingNote: It does not make you win: if the game is won later (for example by defeating the objective's enemy), the ending shows the adventure's conclusion, then this text, and the points are added to those of the objective. Usually used with a condition, for alternative endings.
eventDialog.winHint: The heroes win: the conclusion and the objective's points appear (written in Objectives), plus the pieces added with "Add to the ending".
behaviorsDialog.title: Global monster behaviors
behaviorsDialog.intro: Rules that apply to the monsters of the whole adventure, for the Evil One's script and for whoever plays it. If you choose no monster type they apply to all of them; a single monster can ignore them from Customize.
itemDialog.title: Item on the ground
itemDialog.lookHint: Without a look the token is the item's icon. The title, if you write one, is the name shown in the "!" menu and in notifications instead of the item's own.
itemDialog.pickupHint: A hero who stops on the square picks it up from the "!" menu. An event ("Move a ground item") can move it next to the start.
monsterDialog.name: Name (a monster with a name is unique)
monsterDialog.nameHint: Leave empty for the card's monster; for example: Narthak
monsterDialog.traitLevelHint: Replace the X with the level (a number) to add the ability. Without the X the level is 1.
monsterDialog.uniqueHint: A monster with a name cannot be stunned and its name replaces the card's.
monsterDialog.inactiveHint: Until an event activates it, it does not act, is not attacked and has no abilities, but it occupies its squares and blocks movement and sight like an obstacle.
monsterDialog.invincibleHint: Every wound it should take is 0 (hits taken or missed, flame, pits) until an event makes it vulnerable; the armor shield shows ∞. Turning it on adds "All states" to the immunities; turning it off does not remove it.
monsterDialog.onlyHurtByHint: With any other weapon (or bare-handed) the attack is rolled but every wound is 0, fire and pits included. States are stopped by immunities.
monsterDialog.lookHint: Graphics only, also on an active enemy. Stone: jagged outline like a boulder, image without color. Crystal: gem-like outline with facets and light reflections.
monsterDialog.placeObstacleFirst: First put an obstacle with the Obstacles tool.
monsterDialog.behaviorHint: A constraint on where it can stop during the Evil One's turn, the same for the script and for whoever plays it. "Stay put": it never leaves its square. "End the turn next to…": it can move and attack, but always ends next to the chosen obstacle.
monsterDialog.modifiersHint: Enter values, positive or negative, that modify the monster's normal parameters. Remember that some parameters change with the number of players.
monsterDialog.traitsHint: The card's abilities can be removed with the X (they come back with the + button); the others are added by you.
monsterDialog.immunityHint: What it is not sensitive to. "All states" (flame, net, stun, poison) is a separate entry: an event can remove it without deleting the card's immunities.
monsterDialog.lootHint: When it dies it leaves this. Items fall on its square and, if there are several, on the nearby free squares (or go to whoever deals the fatal blow, if they have room).

editor.when.evilTurnStart: When the Evil One's turn begins
eventDialog.evilTurnStartHint: Fires at the start of the Evil One's turn, after the Evil One has recharged Hatred and drawn cards and before the monsters act. It repeats every round, so it is usually paired with a condition ("If").
eventDialog.healHint: The enemy recovers these wounds, never above its maximum (in the board game: discard wound tokens). If it is already at full health or gone, nothing happens.
eventDialog.placeStairsFirst: First place a staircase on the map with the Doors and passages tool.
eventDialog.placeGlyphFirst: First place a glyph on the map with the Glyphs and more tool.
eventDialog.permadeathHint: While it is on, a hero who dies is eliminated: no city, no return to the dungeon. The party still loses the hero's Value; if no hero is left, the Evil One wins.
eventDialog.prob.heal: Choose the enemy and a number of wounds, 1 or more
c.nameECadutoIlGruppo_161f7: {name} has fallen: the party loses {value} Conquest and the hero is eliminated from the game
c.daOraLaMorteDegli_676f3: From now on, heroes' deaths are permanent
c.laMorteDegliEroiNon_b3d3f: Heroes' deaths are no longer permanent
eventDialog.stairsStateHint: Collapsed: both stairs disappear, link line included, and the 1×1 obstacle chosen in the editor (rubble, pit or nothing) takes their place; anyone standing there is moved to a nearby cell if there is an obstacle. Present: the staircase appears. It can be repeated both ways.
eventDialog.glyphStateHint: Off and lit are the usual two states (lighting it by an event gives no Conquest). Blocked is red and pulses like a lit one, but it cannot be lit and nobody can travel from or to it.
eventDialog.prob.setStairs: Choose the staircase and its new state
eventDialog.prob.setGlyph: Choose the glyph and its new state
stairsDialog.title: Staircase
stairsDialog.hint: Applies to the whole staircase (both stairs). While collapsed it does not exist, and the chosen obstacle takes the place of each stair, or nothing for a secret staircase; an event can make it collapse or reappear.
tools.customizeStairs: Customize: tap a stair to change how the staircase starts
c.nameESbalzatoSuUna_955a7: {name} is thrown onto a nearby cell
c.namePuoSpendereEnergyN_46209: {name} can spend {energy:{n}} to remove one marker of a status afflicting them: it will have no effect. Which one?

c.spendiNEnergiaPerAggiungere_fd8cd: Spend {n} energy to add Sweep: the attack also hits all adjacent enemies
c.quandoAttacchiInMischiaPuoi_ea7a1: When you attack in melee you can spend {energy:3} to add the **Sweep** ability to the attack.
c.allInizioDelTuoTurno_64416: At the start of your turn you can spend {energy:2} to **remove** one marker of a status afflicting you: that marker has no effect.
c.ogniCreaturaAmicaConComando_2b27f: Every friendly creature with Command within 3 spaces (itself included) gives +1 damage and +1 range: +{cmd} damage and +{cmd2} range in total
c.ignoraNPuntiDiArmatura_c9a76: ignores {n} of the target's armor points
c.seiImmuneAPauraAll_8baa5: You are **immune** to Fear. At the start of your turn you **recover** 1 wound.
c.guadagniLAbilitaComandoQuando_59bee: You gain the **Command** ability: when a hero within 3 spaces of you (yourself included) attacks, they get **+1 damage** and **+1 range**.
monsterDialog.delayedHint: It isn't there at the start: it takes no spaces, can't be seen and doesn't act. A "Bring an enemy into play" event puts it in play; the space where you place it here doesn't matter if the event picks the token it appears in place of.
eventDialog.enterPieceHint: The enemy (which must have "Enters play later") appears in place of the chosen Encounter token, which disappears; if the space is taken, in the nearest free one. The camera frames it with a short notice.
eventDialog.prob.round: The round must be a whole number from 1 up (or empty)
eventDialog.prob.enterPiece: Choose the enemy that enters play

validator.ev.enterPieceNotDelayed: The enemy that enters play is already on the map from the start: turn on "Enters play later" in Customize
validator.ev.enterPieceMarkerGone: The Encounter token the enemy appears in place of is no longer on the map
validator.delayedOne: An enemy enters play later but no event brings it in: it will never appear
validator.delayedMany: {n} enemies enter play later but no event brings them in: they will never appear
eventDialog.fxRemoveObstacles: Remove the obstacles in an area
eventDialog.removeObstaclesHint: The obstacles of that type in the chosen area (even partly) disappear: they shrink and dissolve, as if draining away. Afterwards the squares can be crossed.
eventDialog.prob.removeObstacles: Choose the area to remove the obstacles from
validator.ev.removeObstaclesNone: The chosen area has no obstacles of that type: the effect does nothing
validator.twinsOne: A twin glyph has no partner: place another one to make the pair, or delete it
validator.twinsMany: {n} pairs of twin glyphs don't have two glyphs: each pair needs both

monsterDialog.traitNumberHint: Replace the X with a number to add the ability.

validator.startBlockedMany: {n} starting squares are occupied by Encounter tokens that block movement: heroes can't start there

eventDialog.endHeroesTurnHint: The heroes who haven't acted yet end their turn (they lose what is left: movement and attacks; anyone who is moving stops) and the Evil One's turn begins right away. After the event's messages. Outside the heroes' turn it does nothing.
validator.ev.endTurnEvilTurn: "End the heroes' turn" fires during the Evil One's turn: it does nothing
validator.ev.endTurnStartArea: "End the heroes' turn" fires when the starting area is revealed, which happens as soon as the heroes are placed: the first turn would end immediately
tools.customizeObstacle: Customize: tap a pit to choose how it behaves (normal, impassable, deadly)
obstacleDialog.title: Pit
obstacleDialog.normalHint: Whoever falls in loses 1 wound (armor doesn't reduce it) and their movement ends there; you climb out for 2 movement points and can jump over.
obstacleDialog.blockedHint: Nobody enters, neither heroes nor monsters, and it can't be jumped over: like water it blocks movement but not sight. No falling.
obstacleDialog.deadlyHint: Whoever falls in dies, whatever their wounds (a hero goes to the city like on any death). It can still be jumped over, for the bravest.
obstacleDialog.wholePit: It applies to the whole pit: connected squares count as one.
eventDialog.killActorHint: The hero who triggered the event (or, if there is none, the one whose turn it is) dies: the group loses Conquest equal to their value, they lose half their money and go to the city, and their turn ends. With permanent death they leave the game.
eventDialog.p.hintZone: First create a trigger zone: in the Events tray, with the charging-base button.
tools.createZoneHint: Create a zone: tap the squares to include (they can be unconnected), then confirm with the check
tools.zoneChoosing: Tap the squares to include: a second tap removes it. Chosen: {n}. Then confirm with the check at the top.
tools.zonesHintEmpty: No zones yet. Press + to create one: a group of squares (even over a pit or an obstacle) that events use as a trigger.
tools.zoneProps: Customize: the action text, the cost and whether it can be used more than once
zoneDialog.title: Zone
zoneDialog.actionExample: For example: Throw in the relic
validator.ev.zoneGone: The chosen zone no longer exists
validator.zoneLooseOne: A zone is not used by any event: nothing would happen in play
validator.zoneLooseMany: {n} zones are not used by any event: nothing would happen in play
validator.zonesOk: All zones are used by an event
eventDialog.fxSetZone: Turn a zone on or off
eventDialog.setZoneHint: A turned-off zone triggers nothing and its entry doesn't appear. Zones are never used up on their own: they are turned off (and on again) only with this effect.
eventDialog.everyStep: At every step onto one of its squares
eventDialog.everyStepHint: By default it fires when the hero enters the zone from outside. With this option it also fires when moving from one square of the zone to another: useful for rooms full of traps.
tools.zonesToggle: Trigger zones: show the zones instead of the events (again to go back to the events)
zoneDialog.hint: If a "A hero uses a zone" event would do something right now (with its conditions met, or with an "Else" branch), the hero finds the entry in the "!" menu when next to one of the zone's squares (even diagonally, with no wall in between) or standing inside; if only the "Else" fires, the cost isn't paid. A zone is never used up on its own: only the "Turn a zone on or off" effect turns it off. It blocks nothing and isn't visible in play.
validator.zoneOffOne: A zone starts turned off but no event turns it on: it will never do anything
validator.zoneOffMany: {n} zones start turned off but no event turns them on: they will never do anything
tools.deleteZones: Delete: a click on a zone removes it (can be undone)
c.lOggettoCresceIValori_b68d6: The item grows: the card values are those of the current level
eventDialog.levelAmount: By how many levels (negative to make it drop)
eventDialog.levelItemHint: The item takes the dice and abilities of the new level (the table is in the item catalog); it never goes past the final level, which is the card's values, or below 0. The card shows the level.
eventDialog.noLeveledItems: No catalog item grows: an item with levels (`levels`) is needed.
eventDialog.prob.levelAmount: The number of levels must be a non-zero whole number
c.eMaledettaNonSiPuo_4053a: It is cursed: it can't be taken off, only handed over
c.nameSubisce1FeritaPer_e2b4f: {name} suffers 1 wound from the curse of {item}
c.nameSubisceWoundsFeritePer_2cc7c: {name} suffers {wounds} wounds from the curse of {item}
eventDialog.fxGiveChosen: A hero of the group's choice receives an item
eventDialog.giveChosenHint: A dialog asks the group who receives the item (with a single hero, they do). A cursed item equips itself; with no room it falls to the ground. Usually tied to "Heroes reveal an area" on the starting area, for the item the game starts with.
eventDialog.prob.giveChosen: Choose the item to hand over
c.ilGruppoSceglieChiComincia_342e5: The group chooses who starts the game with {item}.
c.maledettoNonSiPuoScartare_e5f55: Cursed: it can't be discarded, set down or put in the backpack. It is handed to an adjacent hero for {mov:{cost}}: whoever receives it equips it right away, and the item that makes room for it goes into the backpack.
c.alTermineDelTuoTurno_cbab3: At the end of your turn, if you haven't killed a monster with this item during the turn, you suffer wounds equal to 1/{n} of your maximum wounds: armor doesn't reduce them.
itemMods.title: Custom items
itemMods.intro: Change a catalog item for this adventure only: growing levels, different values, a curse. The catalog stays untouched.
itemMods.pick: Pick an item on the left, or add one.
itemMods.cursed: Cursed (can't be discarded, only handed over)
itemMods.giveCost: Cost to hand it over (movement points)
itemMods.cursedHint: Whoever receives it equips it at once; whatever it displaces goes to the backpack.
itemMods.curseHint: At the end of the turn, if the hero hasn't killed a monster with the item, they take those wounds (armor doesn't reduce them).
itemMods.invalid: Check the costs and the spark abilities.
tools.itemModsHint: Custom items: change a catalog item for this adventure only
validator.itemLevelsIdleOne: An item with levels is never grown by any event.
validator.itemLevelsIdleMany: {n} items with levels are never grown by any event.
validator.ev.levelItemNoLevels: The item to grow has no levels: set them up in Custom items.
graphics.title: Graphics
graphics.hint: On a computer with little memory, "Light" helps a lot. The choice applies the next time you open the editor or a game.
c.leScintilleDellArmaWeapon_12f95: The sparks of the {weapon} have no effect on you.
itemMods.protectHint: Whoever wears it is unaffected by these weapons' sparks: they can't be paid against them (normal damage still applies).
behavior.useItem: Attacks with an item like a hero
monsterDialog.useItemHint: It attacks with the weapon's dice and sparks, plus these black dice for its attack type: range comes from the roll, as for a hero. The weapon isn't added to its equipment.
monsterDialog.modeAlternate: Alternating rounds with its normal attack
monsterDialog.modeAlternateHint: Odd rounds (1, 3, 5…) it attacks with the item, even rounds with its normal attack.
monsterDialog.modeRandomHint: Each round, half the time, it uses the item; otherwise its normal attack. The choice holds for the whole round. If the enemy has no attack of its own, it always uses the item.
